items.title: Lou Marini interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 15, 2023
items.q: I remember when I met my Spanish wife and she asked me

ctx.x: It is. Have you ever had an instance where you were leading a big band and they were playing your music and a soloist sounded like they were practicing what they were working on during their solo, and it seemed to be a disconnect to the piece itself?

Yeah but you know most of the time it’s rare to get instrumental players that, especially you know like usually the true improviser is a guitar player who has been playing along with records and he’s a rock & roller, but he at least has the idea of a connection between singing in your head and playing what you hear. And yeah, sometimes kids learn — you realize that they’re practicing a solo and trying to play by rote. But at least they’ve made © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-

the effort to try to get somewhere with it you know. And then you hear kids — I heard a 16-year-old alto player — I wonder what he’s doing now, it’s been like eight or nine years ago, from Seattle area, who was in a really fine high school big band and this cat was already, he was a bad ass. And his mother came to me afterwards and she said, “You know his grades are slipping. He was a straight A student, he’s starting to get Bs.” And I said, “You know you’re standing in front of a freight train at this point…
